page: Microsoft Azure FX48ms_v2 is a compute-focused and memory-dense virtual machine within the FXmsv2 series, hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a base clock of 4.2 GHz across 24 physical cores and 48 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled. It includes a sizable 260 MB L3 cache alongside hardware support for vector and matrix extensions including AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8. Memory capacity is substantial at 1008 GB of RAM, providing 21 GB per core. The server includes zero bundled local storage and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote network storage such as Azure Premium Storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational and memory subsystem performance. The high 4.2 GHz clock rate yields top-tier Geekbench single-core scores of 2357.0, with multi-core scores reaching 20288.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 70644.51. Memory throughput is robust, showing 331.05 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 157.25 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks. This architecture delivers high transaction throughput in data handling, recording 76.26 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 28799.79 in PassMark database operations. For machine learning tasks utilizing AMX and AVX instructions, prompt processing reaches strong tiers across various model sizes, though sequential token generation remains in the average tier.

The primary tradeoff of the FX48ms_v2 is the total absence of ephemeral local disk space, meaning all I/O workloads depend entirely on external attached storage volumes. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high ratio of 21 GB RAM per vCPU combined with high single-core frequencies eliminates the need to overprovision core counts purely to acquire large memory footprints. The instance fits in-memory databases like Redis or SAP HANA, large relational database engines, electronic design automation (EDA), financial modeling, and memory-bound batch analytics.

It is equipped with 1008 GB of system memory, delivering a high 21 GB per core allocation. The instance features no bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached storage options. Benchmark testing shows top-tier single-core execution with a Geekbench score of 2357.0, alongside strong uncached memory read bandwidth of 331.05 GB/sec and 76.26 million Redis SET operations per second. The lack of integrated disks requires external storage planning, but the large memory-to-core ratio allows high efficiency for memory-heavy computing without requiring excessive vCPU scaling. The FX48ms_v2 is suited for large in-memory databases, electronic design automation, batch data processing, and financial simulations.
